rationale: Lycopolitan qualitative + 3sg.f object suffix; likely from ⲧⲁⲗⲟ 'mount, raise upon' or ⲱⲗ 'lift, carry.' Used here of the living projection (Cross of Light) being mounted upon the kindled fire. Cf. ⲧⲁⲗⲏⲩ 'be exalted/mounted' in accumulated vocabulary.

Causative-perfect verb with 3sg.f object suffix, used twice in this kephalaion (lines 12, 16) of the cosmic kindling of fire — 'they kindled her [= the fire] forth from the powers of light' / 'they kindled her forth from the All.' Likely Lyc reflex of ⲥⲁⲧⲉ/ⲥⲁⲧⲡ̄ 'set on fire' or related ignition-verb.

Lycopolitan reflex of standard Coptic idiom ⲕⲱ ⲁϩⲏⲩ 'leave naked, set bare.' Used here of the cosmic-divine moment when the descending one strips himself of his prior investiture before standing before the Omophoros.

Pairs with ⲡⲟⲗⲉⲙⲟⲥ 'war' as a doublet-couplet for cosmic conflict. Etymology unclear — possibly Lyc reflex of a martial-conflict noun, or a corrupt form. Confidence low; flagged for parallel attestations.
Editor's restored prefix in [ⲫⲉ]ⲙⲉⲗⲟⲥ. Likely Lycopolitan possessive ⲡϩⲉ- 'his' (cf. ⲡⲉϩ- in accumulated vocabulary) with ⲡϩ→ⲫ assimilation, or a definite-article variant.
